subject: Post-call: Structured output reliability & integration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Structured output reliability & integration next steps

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: embed generative responses into Acme's support assistant with structured JSON output for downstream tooling and safe reranking with embeddings.
- Primary concerns you raised: reliable JSON-constrained decoding, validation + retry patterns, authentication and routing across envs (hosted now, private VPC later), and embedding/reranker latency.

Action items / integration checklist we discussed:
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Recommend starting with Redwood JS SDK (node) + API key for PoC. For production (VPC) we can switch to short-lived tokens / OIDC.
2) Routing & model selection
   - Route low-latency requests to hosted Redwood endpoints; add fallback policy to smaller quantized model for heavy concurrency.
3) Structured output reliability
   - Use a strict JSON schema + constrained decoding (token biasing / grammar) and server-side JSON validation.
   - Implement a 2-step pattern: (a) model generates JSON; (b) validation service checks schema + field-level checks; if invalid, automatic retry with clarified prompt + higher temperature constraint off.
4) Embeddings & reranking
   - Create dense embedding index of KB; perform candidate retrieval + rerank locally to limit model tokens and improve determinism.

Questions for your engineering team (please reply inline):
- Which auth method is in your near-term roadmap (API keys / OAuth/OIDC / Okta)?
- Expected qps and 95th percentile latency requirements for the assistant (rough numbers)?
- Do you have an existing schema we should conform to for the structured output, or should we propose a starting JSON schema?

Next suggested steps:
- You share the current schema + any security constraints (e.g., data residency, IP allowlist).
- We set a 60-minute technical sync: internal SE (Neha), SRE/architecture (Vivek) + your infra lead to walk auth and routing.
- We'll provide a short draft of the JSON schema and a sample validation + retry pattern doc (I'll attach the checklist).

Attachments: acme-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration items + owners).

Thanks — looking forward to the answers so we can schedule the tech sync.

—
Marissa Cole

Marissa — quick internal notes before we sync with Acme: 
- Based on the call, Acme plans to use Okta for identity; they mentioned OAuth for other apps. If they confirm Okta, we should prepare OIDC short-lived token instructions and an example Okta app manifest.
- Embeddings: they want reranking to reduce hallucinations. We should propose an initial candidate set size (k=10) and an offline evaluation plan.
- Vivek: looping you in — please advise on any VPC-specific routing considerations for constrained-decoding (tokenization determinism across quantized models).

I can draft the JSON schema proposal; Marissa, if you can push for their current schema from Alex that'd speed things up.

-Neha

Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Structured output reliability & integration next steps

Marissa / team — thanks for the summary. Answers inline below and a couple of notes:

Q: Auth method
A: Short term: we want to use Okta/OAuth for our platform (SSO). For the PoC we can accept API keys inside our backend service but we'll want a migration plan to OIDC tokens for the VPC deployment. Attached: acme-okta-config.pdf (Okta app details).

Q: Traffic & latency expectations
A: Initial scope: 50 concurrent sessions, target P95 < 1s for the ranking path and P95 < 800ms for structured JSON generation (we understand some tradeoffs).

Q: Schema
A: We don't have a finalized schema yet. We do have an internal response envelope we use for other microservices (see short snippet below). We'll attach the envelope spec and a sample payload. Please propose a stricter schema for the model output (field types, enums, required vs optional).

On retries & validation: our infra team is cautious about repeated model calls for cost reasons. Would you recommend doing a lightweight local syntax + type validation first, then for failures attempt one model-level retry with a constrained prompt and lower temperature? Also curious if Redwood has a preferred way to annotate which fields are critical and which can be fuzzy.

Attachments included: acme-okta-config.pdf, acme-response-envelope.json (sample).

Happy to schedule the tech sync next week — we can do Tue or Thu mornings PST.

—Alex
Lead Product Engineer, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Structured output reliability & integration next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the details and attachments. Next steps from our side: 

1) Neha will draft a proposed JSON schema (including enum values + required fields) and a validation flow (local schema check -> model-aware retry with constrained prompt -> fallback to safe default) by EOD Friday.
2) Vivek will prepare a short note on VPC routing and token exchange patterns for Okta/OIDC and confirm any determinism notes for quantized kernels.
3) I'll schedule the 60-minute tech sync for Tue 2026-08-11 10:00 AM PST (placeholder) — calendar invite to follow; please flag conflicts.

Proposed validation + retry pattern (short):
- Step A: Model returns JSON. Immediately run a JSON schema validator (fast, local).
- Step B: If schema fails, classify errors (missing required, wrong type, enum mismatch). For minor enum/type issues, attempt a programmatic normalization. For structural failures, perform exactly one automated model retry with a stricter instruction: provide the previous (invalid) JSON, the schema, and explicit constraints (max tokens, temperature 0.0, token bias to disallow stray punctuation).
- Step C: If retry still fails, log the failure and apply a deterministic fallback (e.g., return the last-known-good record or escalate to human review depending on field criticality).

I'll upload Neha's draft and Vivek's note to the Drive folder and share the link here once available: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmeIntegration

Thanks — we'll come prepared with the schema draft and a demo harness for the retry pattern at the tech sync.
